// FINDING TEMPLATE -- copy to findings/<ID>.adoc (ID = CVE id, or GHSA id if no CVE).
// Owned by the reviewer of the unit (sweep) that produced it. Rules: appendix-definitions.adoc.
// Every attribute below must be present in every finding (use an empty value where
// optional); findings are included one after another, so an omitted attribute would
// inherit the previous finding's value. tools/review.py reads these attributes to build
// the summary, recommendations and coverage tables -- do not edit those tables by hand.
:finding-id: CVE-YYYY-NNNNN
:finding-aliases: GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx
:finding-title: <short title in Roc-reader terms>
:finding-track: <A or B>
:finding-sweep: <sweep-id of the unit that produced this finding>
:finding-component: <inventory row or attack-surface class, exactly as in the SUT tables>
:finding-location: <`src/path.zig`, `symbol`>
:finding-outcome: <Track A: not_affected, affected, fixed, under_investigation; Track B: pattern absent, weakness possible, weakness confirmed, hardening candidate, undetermined>
:finding-justification: <Track A not_affected only: one of the five VEX justifications; else empty>
:finding-scope: <e.g. (Windows hosts only); else empty>
:finding-cwe: <CWE-NNN, Base or Variant>
:finding-ssvc: <Immediate, Out-of-Cycle, Scheduled, Defer, or n/a where no priority is required>
:finding-ssvc-points: <Exploitation: x; Utility: x; Technical Impact: x; Public Safety Impact: x (tree version)>
:finding-upstream-score: <CVSS-B x.y or CVSS v3.1 x.y; EPSS x (date); KEV yes/no>
:finding-about: <one sentence: what the upstream bug is>
:finding-ask: <one sentence: what, if anything, contributors are asked to do>
:finding-action: <fix, investigate, add regression test, add fuzz target, accept risk, no action>
:finding-action-detail: <one sentence; empty for no action>
:finding-owner: unassigned
:finding-status: draft
:finding-assessed-by: <agent/model or person>

[[cve-yyyy-nnnnn]]
= {finding-id}: {finding-title}

[cols="1,3"]
|===
|Aliases |{finding-aliases}
|Track |{finding-track}
|Roc component |{finding-component}: {finding-location}
|Outcome |{finding-outcome} {finding-justification} {finding-scope}
|CWE |{finding-cwe}
|Priority (SSVC) |{finding-ssvc}. {finding-ssvc-points}
|Upstream score |{finding-upstream-score} (context only)
|Assessed |at `{roc-commit}` by {finding-assessed-by}
|===

// Track B only (required by tools/review.py):
IMPORTANT: This CVE affects the cited upstream product; this record does not assert that this project has the same vulnerability.

== For contributors
// 3-5 plain sentences, written last: the upstream bug, what the corresponding Roc code or
// contract does, the outcome, and what (if anything) is asked.

== References
// The CVE record first, then the vendor advisory, OSV/NVD, and the fix commit, as URL[label], with access dates.

== Upstream facts
// Product (PURL), affected range (OSV events), fix commit, root cause, impact, record state, disputes.

== Claims

// One row per line. Label: Examined-code | Examined-source | Tested | Inferred | Unverified.
// Examined-code evidence MUST be: <pinned link>[`path:n`]: `exact text from line n`
// tools/review.py checks that the quoted text appears at that line at {roc-commit}.
[cols="1,4,2,4",options="header"]
|===
|# |Claim |Label |Evidence
|C1 | |Examined-code |https://github.com/roc-lang/roc/blob/<sha>/src/path.zig#L1[`src/path.zig:1`]: `exact quoted text`
|===

== Root cause and exposure path
// Track A: version -> built in -> reachable -> adversary control, each step citing a claim.
// Track B: the Roc lines that embody (or refute) the pattern, compared with the upstream fix.
// Contract: whether the weakness is in the specification or only in Roc's implementation.

== Counter-evidence searched

== Unverified claims and the checks that would settle them

== Assessment
// Outcome via appendix-definitions.adoc; impact statement (not_affected) or action statement
// (affected); SSVC decision points with a rationale each; SP 800-30 narrative.

== Recommendation

== Conditions that would change this outcome
